answer: Each epoch, an identity appears at a seed- and key-derived moment and signs the live head: a comet, unreplayable if missed. An operator with N identities cannot serve them serially — moments collide, overlap growing as N squared — so the attacker buys peak concurrent sessions, not more prompts: a price rising faster than the count. Each appearance emits a pulse; identities on one scheduler pulse in phase — a shared clock betrays one operator. Each pulse carries a pigment, a key-derived mark: one identity stays self-consistent, two from one generator smear to one colour. Timing exposes them.
